subject: Post-demo: hosting preference and migration path decision points for Atlas Health
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Leah Park <l.park@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-18T15:20:00-08:00
Subject: Post-demo: hosting preference and migration path decision points for Atlas Health

Hi Leah —

Thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap and the open items we promised to track:

Summary of ask
- Atlas wants predictable latency for patient-facing summarization (95th percentile < 300ms).
- Strong data residency & audit requirements for PHI (on-prem or VPC preferred).
- Migration: you have an existing self-hosted cluster running a mixture of legacy GPUs + a small set of API calls through another provider.

What we recommend (high-level)
- Short-term: Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) to hit latency + audit controls while keeping control plane in your VPC.
- Mid-term: Private (customer-managed control plane on VPC or on-prem package) if you require fully air-gapped storage for PHI.
- Fallback: Hosted API for burst traffic and dev sandbox.

Open questions (please confirm):
1) Are there procurement constraints that force a single vendor/contract for infra (PO vs. SOW)?
2) Do you have a KMS / HSM vendor preference for key management?
3) Can you share a rough qps profile and peak concurrency for user-facing LLM calls? (ballpark numbers are fine)

Attachments: ATLAS_POC_REQUIREMENTS.xlsx (stub) — includes the call notes I typed up; feel free to mark edits.

Proposed next steps
- Ben and I will produce a short-fit summary (Dedicated vs Private) with cost/latency tradeoffs by Monday.
- If procurement wants, we can produce a one-page SOW + PO template that maps to Dedicated onboarding milestones.
- Suggest a technical sync (infra + security) next week to validate network/VPC requirements.

Thanks —
Priyom
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priom.das@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Leah Park <l.park@atlashealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Atlas Health Procurement <procurement@atlashealth.com>
Date: 2026-02-18T18:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: hosting preference and migration path decision points for Atlas Health

Thanks, Priyom — great summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Procurement: we like to start with a PO for the initial POC (90 days) and then move to an annual committed reserved capacity contract for production. Procurement is on this thread.

2) KMS: we currently use an internal HashiCorp Vault setup integrated with our HSM provider. We will need Redwood to support external KMS integration (bring-your-own) or key wrapping.

3) Traffic: current baseline is ~15 qps across inference endpoints during peak hours; peaks can spike to ~60 qps for short bursts (licensing-checks, heavier summarization).

4) Migration constraints: our infra team (cc Rajiv Mehra, external consultant) warns that our legacy GPU cluster is not reliable for horizontal autoscaling. We want a migration path that avoids re-architecting all upstream batch jobs. Ideally we lift traffic to Dedicated first and then cut over gradually.

5) Compliance: Atlas requires an audit log of inference calls (token-level logging acceptable if kept in customer-owned S3).

Please include the procurement contact for the PO template. We also attached a short matrix (ATLAS_POC_REQUIREMENTS.xlsx) with compliance items filled out.

—Leah
Head of Data Products | Atlas Health
leah.park@atlashealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Leah Park <l.park@atlashealth.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-19T01:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: hosting preference and migration path decision points for Atlas Health

Leah — thanks for the details. Quick technical notes that map to your items: 

- KMS: Redwood Private supports external KMS integrations (Vault + HSM). For Dedicated we can offer customer-managed key wrapping via KMS proxies; I'll include the integration checklist.

- Latency & capacity: with the 15 qps baseline and 60 qps burst profile, recommended starting point is a Dedicated cluster with 4x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved) + burst pool on hosted. That configuration hits ~95th pctl < 250ms on our benchmarks for your expected model sizes.

- Migration path (practical):
  1) POC using Dedicated in your VPC (single subnet) with ingress control to mirror traffic for 2 weeks.
  2) Gradual cutover of read calls (summaries) while keeping batch jobs on legacy cluster.
  3) Once performance & logs validated, flip production routing and decommission legacy APIs incrementally.

- Audit logs: we support token-level telemetry; for PHI you can choose to store logs in customer-owned S3 and enable envelope encryption.

Attachments: POC-Infra-Checklist.xlsx (stub) — includes ports, subnets, nginx sidecar suggestion, and required IAM roles.

Action for Priyom: can you confirm procurement timeline and whether Atlas needs a SOW + PO or will accept a PO alone for the POC?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Leah Park <l.park@atlashealth.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Atlas Health Procurement <procurement@atlashealth.com>, Rajiv Mehra <r.mehra@legacygpu.com>
Date: 2026-02-19T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: hosting preference and migration path decision points for Atlas Health

Leah / Team — appreciate the quick responses. A few concrete next steps so this doesn't stall: 

1) Procurement contact: Leah, please intro the PO contact (email) or loop someone from procurement on a follow-up mail. If you prefer we can draft a short PO-ready statement of work that lists the POC milestones (network setup, compliance checklist, performance validation).

2) Technical sync: propose a 45-min call Monday 2026-02-23 10:00 AM PT. Agenda: network/VPC specifics, KMS handshake, and sampling plan for audit logs. Please confirm availability.

3) Deliverables we will send by Monday EOD:
- One-page Dedicated vs Private recommendation with estimated cost ranges (for 12-month commit and POC PO).
- Draft POC SOW + PO template you can hand to procurement.
- POC-Infra-Checklist.xlsx (attached) for your infra team to pre-fill.

4) Contract nuance: for the 90-day POC we typically accept a PO only if the customer is comfortable with auto-renew path to reserved capacity; otherwise the SOW + PO combo works better for procurement visibility. We can make the POC cancellation and data-retention terms explicit.

Please reply with: procurement contact + confirmation for Monday call. If Monday doesn't work we can do Tuesday morning as an alternative.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai
